acceptedRisks.rationale: Neither the key-rotation drill nor the isolated restore has been rehearsed, and this ships without them. It is acceptable on day one because its absence harms no user directly: nothing in the product is degraded by a drill not having been run. What is unknown is recovery time. If a key leaks or the database needs restoring, the first attempt will be the rehearsal, under pressure, at an unmeasured duration. Mitigations that exist: every migration is additive and re-runnable, Supabase retains automated backups, the rollback path is flag-based, and MW-V12-05 added a per-secret procedure, a safe fingerprint check and an executable restore verification so the drill is now scripted rather than improvised. Standing 2026-07-28 acceptance carried into the v12 candidate; to be re-confirmed and reviewed before the paid tier scales beyond the initial cohort.

No charge has been captured against the live 9.99 EUR plan, and cancel, reactivate, recovery and refund have never been exercised live. What is verified is narrower: the live prices read back 999 and 5999 eur, and live trial checkout completes. The owner judges the remaining risk acceptable because the first paying customers are a small known cohort he can refund by hand, and because the currency defect that made this dangerous is closed. MW-V12-03 additionally made the out-of-order and late payment_failed-after-recovery path safe in code, so the specific residual that could silently remove access is now guarded and unit-tested; the live refund path is still unproven. Accepted deliberately rather than closed. Standing 2026-07-28 acceptance carried into the v12 candidate; to be rehearsed before the cohort grows beyond people the owner can contact directly.

No authenticated journey is red; what keeps this open is that the full matrix has never executed unattended in one pass at a single SHA, because it needs a seeded non-production Supabase. MW-V12-02 turned this from a coverage-completeness worry into a runnable, fail-closed step: a canonical matrix, a runner that BLOCKS on any required journey that never ran, an integrity test that stops a required test from silently vanishing, and an opt-in marker guard so the seed cannot be pointed at production. The gap is now purely that the owner has not yet run it against an env. Standing 2026-07-28 acceptance carried into the v12 candidate; to be run before anyone other than the owner uses the suite.

Five of seven acceptance items were evidenced live on 2026-07-28. The two that remained — a duplicate eligible cron run and a deliberate provider failure — are covered by deterministic unit tests and, in MW-V12-04, sharpened in the owner worksheet so the live run isolates the dedupe key and observes the retry/backoff/dead-letter transitions rather than proving nothing. The consequence if either is wrong is a duplicate or missing reminder email, not a loss of access or money, which is why this is accepted where the untested paths are narrow and the blast radius is one email. Standing 2026-07-28 acceptance carried into the v12 candidate.

rollback: Flag-based and data-safe. FLAG_MONTHLY_FAIR_USE=0, FLAG_PLAN_REPAIR=0, FLAG_WEEKLY_REFLECTION=0, FLAG_EMPHASIZE_YEARLY unset, FLAG_TRIAL_LENGTH_EXPERIMENT=0 (pinned trials complete exactly as disclosed; no subscription is touched), plus per-surface UI reverts. Every migration in the repository is additive and re-runnable, so no migration reversal is required to roll back any behaviour; migrations 040 and 041 are additive columns/tables and the app tolerates their absence.
